- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots downward — reduce forecast dip by 10–20% of the spike magnitude.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 50% of recent high), model tends to lag — add 1–2 days of gradual upward correction.  
- When sentiment is positive but model forecasts are flat or falling, model underestimates rebound — increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility — add 1–2% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is volatile or trending.
